summary: Akira Mukai specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his doctoral studies at Hokkaido University, where he served as an assistant from ~1972 to 1979, and was later attested as a professor at Hokkaido Musashi Women's Junior College in 1999.

Akira Omine worked in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies, earning degrees at Kyoto University and studying at Heidelberg University. His career included posts at Kyoto University, Osaka University of Foreign Studies, Osaka University, Ryukoku University, and the Shinshu Otaniha Institute.

Akira Sadakata works in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Akira Hirakawa and Hajime Nakamura, and at the University of Paris. His main academic career was at Tokai University as associate professor, professor, and professor emeritus.

Akira Saitō is a Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Jikidō Takasaki and at Australian National University. He held professorships at the University of Tokyo, Mie University, and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies.

Akira Shimada specializes in history, archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the College of Art, Delhi under Rajeev Lochan and Daud Ali, and held posts at the British Museum and the State University of New York at New Paltz.

Akira Suganuma specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed doctoral studies at Toyo University, where he served as assistant (~1962–1965) and associate professor (1991–1994), and also lectured at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies in 1981.
Akira Unete works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. His academic posts include associate professor at Otani University, attested in 2010, and faculty at the Otani Academic Society, attested in 2026.

Akira Yuyama specialized in Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics, studying at Leiden and under Jan Willem de Jong and Arthur Llewellyn Basham. He held posts at the Australian National University, International Institute for Buddhist Studies, and Soka University.

Akitoshi Saito worked in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He served as a professor and later professor emeritus at Taisho University, and was attested as an advisor at the Kawasaki Daishi Research Institute of Buddhist Studies in 2014.
Akong Tulku Rinpoche was a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. In 1967, he founded the Kagyu Samye Ling Monastery and Tibetan Centre, where he served as abbot.
Akshara Ravishankar Parmeswaran works in Indology and philosophy. Parmeswaran is a doctoral candidate at the University of Chicago and is attested as a researcher at Ghent University in 2026.
Akshay Ramanlal Desai was a historian and archaeologist. He studied at the University of Mumbai between ~1937 and 1946 under the supervision of Govind Sadashiv Ghurye.
Alan Entwistle was an Indologist who completed his education at the University of Southampton and SOAS University of London between ~1970 and 1982. He also taught Heidi Rika Maria Pauwels.

Alan Fox specializes in philosophy, religious studies, and Sinology, having completed his PhD at Temple University by 1988. He has served as a professor and associate professor in the Department of Philosophy at the University of Delaware.

Alan Gerard Wagner works in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He completed a PhD at Harvard University under doctoral supervisor Parimal G. Patil, having also studied under Robert M. Gimello, Charles Hallisey, Carl Bielefeldt, and Masatoshi Nagatomi.
Alan Gowans was a scholar in history and archaeology who studied at the University of Toronto (1946) and Princeton University (1948, 1950). He also taught Michael Willis.

Alan John Bayard Wace was an archaeologist and historian educated at Pembroke College under Robert Alexander Neil. His primary posts included the British School at Athens, Victoria and Albert Museum, University of Cambridge, and Alexandria University.

Alan Lomax was an American scholar educated at St. Mark's School of Texas and Choate Rosemary Hall, who subsequently completed studies at Harvard University, the University of Texas at Austin, and Columbia University.
Alan Nussbaum is a linguist and Indologist. He completed his studies at Harvard University between ~1970 and 1976 and served on the faculty at Cornell University from ~1985 to 2022.

Alan Sponberg was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned his PhD from the University of British Columbia. He held teaching posts at Princeton University (attested 1980–1987) and Stanford University (attested 1988).
